info.title: Sess owner API
info.description: Owner API (P0 display Sessions; P1 interactive Sessions). Request bodies are limited to 256 KiB; a Surface measure (UTF-8 bytes of the canonical Surface JSON) above 131072 bytes is rejected with 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE. Every table row must have the same key set. Every JSON response carries Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform. Interactive Sessions: active → responded (one accepted response per revision, response_policy first) → active (the owner publishes the next revision) … → completed (terminal).

ownerKey.description: An owner credential: the deployment owner key (acts in the operator workspace) or a developer API key sess_sk_… from the account pages (acts only in its developer workspace; a revoked or expired key → 401 UNAUTHORIZED). A Session of another workspace is 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND.

managementCredential.description: The trial management credential (sess_mg_…), returned once at trial creation.

startGrant.description: A target start grant (sess_gr_…) issued by the target’s owner; accepted only on POST /v1/invocations, from the grant’s audience Origin.

participantCredential.description: The participant credential (sess_pc_…) a start returns: status and cancel of that one Invocation.

callbackCredential.description: The callback credential (sess_cb_…) of one dispatch, sent only to the verified target.

items.description: One SurfaceComponent (heading, text, record or field). An unrecognized type fails with 400 UNKNOWN_COMPONENT.

response_policy.description: One accepted response per revision (the only P1 policy; the default).

expires_in.description: Advanced. How long the Sess link stays open, in seconds from creation: at least 30 and at most the plan’s live-link lifetime (Free 604800, Starter and Pro 2592000; the deployment owner key 2592000). Absent: the plan’s lifetime. Out of range → 400 INVALID_SCHEMA, whose message names both bounds. Completion never moves the expiry.

invocation_id.description: Advanced. The invocation_id of the run your registered agent received, when this Session serves that run. Sess then records the agent and its version with every receipt it keeps for this Session. The run must be in your workspace and still open: an unknown run → 422 VALIDATION_FAILED (reason unknown_invocation); a run that has ended → 409 INVOCATION_TERMINAL. Absent: the Session is not tied to a run.

action_expires_at.description: The Sess link’s current deadline for answers: an RFC 3339 UTC instant with milliseconds. From this instant the link no longer opens and accepts no response. Set when the Session is created and never extended by a read; never null. For an interactive link of 20 hours or less the person may move it forward by asking for more time, never past action_expires_horizon (see link_state). A link revoked by the operator stops earlier; this field does not report revocation.

action_expires_horizon.description: For an interactive Sess link of 20 hours or less (created with expires_in of 72000 or less, or a trial): the fixed instant after which the link can never be extended or reopened, set when the Session is created: creation + the original lifetime + 10 × min(original lifetime, 1 hour). It never moves. null for a link longer than 20 hours, a display Session, or a Session created before link extensions existed: their links end at action_expires_at.

extensions_used.description: How many times the person extended the link (at most 10). Each extension moves action_expires_at forward by min(original lifetime, 1 hour), never past action_expires_horizon. Always 0 when action_expires_horizon is null.

link_state.description: The Sess link’s state at the time of this read. live: it opens and accepts answers (before action_expires_at). lapsed: past action_expires_at, but the person can still ask for more time until action_expires_horizon; it accepts no answer and does not open, and the Session is still open for your agent: keep waiting. expired: it will never accept an answer (at the horizon, once the deadline passes with no extensions left, on revocation, or after the deadline of a completed Session). Revoke the link when you need a hard end at the deadline. An answer accepted while live stays the result.

get.description: The developer sign-in page: an email field and an explicit, unticked "Remember this device" box (remember=1) whose form (POST, same-origin only) requests a sign-in email. A request from this page is one challenge: a link and a six-digit code (P2 D2(a)), with a random browser challenge in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, host-only cookie (Path=/app, 15 minutes) that the code is bound to; then 303 to /app/check-email, whose code form posts to /app/sign-in/code. With a live account session (unexpired, not revoked) the answer is 303 to /app/keys, a fixed internal path that nothing in the request can change. With a pending key creation (a valid key-intent cookie) the page is always shown, re-titled "Verify it’s you", whatever the session: that key is created only after the email link is confirmed. When GitHub sign-in is configured (P2 D2(b)) the page also has "Continue with GitHub" (POST /app/sign-in/github), and then its form-action also allows https://github.com. Reading this page never consumes a link, creates a key or changes anything.

200.description: The sign-in page (no live account session, or a pending key creation waiting for verification).

303.description: A live account session: to /app/keys.

get.description: The page the emailed link opens (the token is a single-use secret; never log it). It only shows a Sign in button (with ?continue=key, a link requested to finish a key creation: "Continue creating your key"); it consumes nothing.

post.description: Consumes the link once (same-origin requests only), which also ends the code of the same challenge, and sets the account-page cookie: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, host-only, Path=/app, 12 hours, or 30 days when "Remember this device" was chosen and the link is confirmed in the browser that chose it (absolute: never extended). A previous session of this browser is revoked. When the same browser holds a pending key creation of the same account (the key-intent cookie, set by a create post with an expired session of that account), the key is created now with that label and expiry, once, and the response is the one-time reveal; the intent cookie is cleared. A pending creation of another account creates nothing.

200.description: Signed in; the pending key was not created because the expiry date its form showed is no longer the date a key created now would get (a new UTC day began): the keys page with a fresh form.

201.description: Signed in and the pending key created: the keys page with it, shown once.

303.description: Signed in: to /app/keys (/app/keys?resume=elsewhere when the link was for a key creation started in another browser), with Set-Cookie.

400.description: SIGN_IN_LINK_INVALID: expired, used or replaced by a newer link.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin request.

409.description: Signed in; the pending key was not created: KEY_LIMIT_REACHED (the account has 10 active keys).

post.description: Redeems the emailed six-digit sign-in code (P2 D2(a)) in the browser that requested it. Form fields: csrf (the check-email page’s token, derived from the browser challenge) and code (6 digits; spaces and hyphens are ignored). Same-origin form posts only. The code works for 10 minutes and for at most 5 guesses per challenge; failed guesses also count, across resends, toward per-address (10), per-client (30) and global (2000) limits per rolling hour. A match consumes the challenge atomically (its link stops working) and then behaves as POST /app/confirm/{token}: the session cookie (12 hours, or 30 days when "Remember this device" was chosen), and a pending key creation of the same account in this browser is created and shown once. Every refusal is the same answer.

201.description: Signed in and the pending key created: the keys page with it, shown once.

303.description: Signed in: to /app/keys (/app/keys?resume=elsewhere for a key creation started in another browser or account), with Set-Cookie.

400.description: SIGN_IN_CODE_INVALID: the same answer for a wrong, expired, used, replaced or locked code, an unknown or missing browser challenge, a full guess limit or a malformed entry.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin form post, or a wrong CSRF token.

post.description: Signs out one remembered device of the signed-in account (P2 D2(a)), listed with its public id (acs_…) under "Sign-in and sessions" on /app/keys. Same-origin form posts with the session’s CSRF token only. Signing out this device clears its cookie.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: cross-origin or a wrong CSRF token.

404.description: NOT_FOUND: not a signed-in device of this account.

post.description: Starts a GitHub account sign-in (P2 D2(b)): "Continue with GitHub" on /app/sign-in, shown only when the deployment has a GitHub OAuth app (SESS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and SESS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET). Same-origin form posts only. A new random state (256 bits, stored only as its hash, single use, 10 minutes) is bound to a new browser binding secret in the __Secure-sess_github cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, host-only, Path=/app, 10 minutes; stored only as its hash), which also derives the PKCE verifier (never stored or sent to the browser). The answer is 303 to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with client_id, the fixed redirect_uri <account origin>/app/sign-in/github/callback, scope=user:email (the only scope), state, code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256. Optional field return: /keys (default) or /evidence; anything else is /keys. At most 30 starts per client and 1000 in total per rolling hour. A page with this form also allows https://github.com in form-action; every other account page keeps form-action 'self'.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin form post.

get.description: Where GitHub sends the browser back (the callback URL registered with the OAuth app). GET reads only: with a well-formed code and state, a "Finish signing in with GitHub" page whose Continue button posts them back (same origin); GitHub’s own error (error=access_denied when the person cancelled) is shown as such. The code and state are single-use secrets: the request log carries the route pattern only, never the query.

400.description: GITHUB_SIGN_IN_CANCELLED (the person cancelled on GitHub) or GITHUB_SIGN_IN_FAILED (GitHub’s error, or a malformed code or state).

503.description: SIGN_IN_UNAVAILABLE: GitHub sign-in is not configured.

post.description: Finishes a GitHub sign-in or link in the browser that started it. Form fields: code and state. Same-origin form posts only, carrying the __Secure-sess_github binding cookie whose hash the state is bound to: the state is used once, whatever happens next (a replay, another browser or a planted callback finds it used or unbound). Then the code is exchanged at GitHub with the PKCE verifier, the stable numeric GitHub user ID and the verified primary address are read with user:email, and the GitHub access token is discarded (never stored or logged). A sign-in: a linked GitHub ID signs in to its account (whatever the address or login now); a new ID with a verified, usable primary address that no account has creates an account and its link; an address that an existing account has is never merged (GITHUB_NOT_LINKED: sign in with email, then link); no verified usable address leads to the email sign-in (nothing created). Signing in opens a new 12-hour account session exactly as the email sign-in does (the cookie policy is the same; the browser’s previous session is revoked) and continues a pending key creation of the same account in this browser. A link: only the account session that started it, still live and signed in within 12 hours, links; a GitHub account links to one Sess account and an account to one GitHub account.

200.description: GITHUB_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED: GitHub shared no verified, usable primary address; the sign-in page with the email form. Nothing was created.

201.description: Signed in and the pending key created: the keys page with it, shown once.

303.description: Signed in: to the allowlisted return (/app/keys or /app/evidence; /app/keys?resume=elsewhere for a key creation of another account), with Set-Cookie. Linked: to /app/keys?github=linked.

400.description: GITHUB_SIGN_IN_FAILED: the same answer for an unknown, used, expired or altered state, a missing or other browser binding, and a code GitHub refused.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED (not a same-origin form post), or for a link RECENT_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED / GITHUB_SIGN_IN_FAILED (the session is not the one that started it, or its sign-in is more than 12 hours old).

409.description: GITHUB_NOT_LINKED (a sign-in whose address an existing account has), GITHUB_ALREADY_LINKED (a link of a GitHub account another account has) or GITHUB_LINK_EXISTS (this account already has another GitHub account).

post.description: Starts linking a GitHub account to the signed-in account (P2 D2(b)), from "Sign-in and sessions" on /app/keys. Same-origin form posts with the session’s CSRF token only, and a sign-in within the last 12 hours. Then exactly as POST /app/sign-in/github, with the state also bound to this account and session.

post.description: Unlinks the account’s GitHub account (P2 D2(b)). Same-origin form posts with the session’s CSRF token only, and a sign-in within the last 12 hours. Every other live session that GitHub account opened is signed out; this one goes on. The account always keeps its email sign-in, so unlinking never leaves it without a way in. Works even when GitHub sign-in is no longer configured.

303.description: Unlinked: to /app/keys?github=unlinked. No live account session: to /app/sign-in.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED (cross-origin or a wrong CSRF token) or RECENT_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED (signed in more than 12 hours ago).

post.description: Creates an owner API key (sess_sk_…) of the developer workspace and shows it once, in one post of the keys page’s create form. The form states each expiry choice’s exact date and carries a single-use nonce bound to the account session (15 minutes); creating consumes it, so a refresh or repeat never creates a second key or shows the secret again. The stored expiry has the date the form showed (rendered_at, bound to the nonce); when that date is no longer true the form is shown again (400). Form fields: csrf (the page’s token), nonce, rendered_at, label (optional, ≤ 64 characters, no control characters), expires_in_days (30, 90, 365 or never; required). Same-origin requests with the session’s CSRF token only. At most 10 active keys per account. With an expired account session (same-origin posts only), a valid label and expiry choice, bound to that account, is kept in a key-intent cookie (HMAC-protected, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, host-only, Path=/app, 15 minutes) and the answer is 303 to /app/sign-in ("Verify it’s you"); the key is created only after the email link is confirmed in the same browser. A live session whose sign-in is more than 12 hours old (a remembered device) is treated the same way: revealing a new key needs a recent email verification. Revoke: POST /app/keys/{id}/revoke (same rules), immediate. Sign out: POST /app/sign-out.

303.description: No live account session, or a sign-in more than 12 hours old: to /app/sign-in (with the key-intent cookie for a valid choice).

400.description: INVALID_SCHEMA: an expiry that is not offered, an invalid label (the field shows the error), a form nonce that is missing, unknown, expired or issued to another account session, a changed rendered_at, or expiry dates that changed since the form was shown.

P2-12 B3: with billing configured, the Change plan section (Checkout from Free, an in-place change for a subscribed workspace, Manage billing) and the plan badge; at the limit a link to Change plan beside the reason. Query billing (a fixed notice code after a billing action) is display only. Its CSP form-action also allows the payment provider’s hosted Checkout and portal origins. Without a live account session: 303 to /app/sign-in.

303.description: To /app/sign-in.

post.description: P2-12 B3: changes the signed-in developer workspace’s paid plan. Form fields: csrf (the page’s token) and plan (starter or pro; the server selects the approved price, nothing else comes from the browser). Same-origin requests with the session’s CSRF token only. Without a subscription: a hosted Checkout (the same one as POST /v1/account/billing/checkout), answered 303 to the provider’s Checkout page. With a subscription: its one subscription changes in place (never a second subscription or a new Checkout), which needs a sign-in within the last 12 hours; the plan changes only when the provider’s verified subscription state shows it (a signed event or reconciliation), never from this request. An uncertain provider outcome is never success: the change stays pending and the next request replays it under the same idempotency key before anything else is sent.

303.description: To the provider’s hosted Checkout page; or to /app/usage?billing=<notice> with notice requested, unchanged, payment_required, reauth, not_changeable, ending, processing, busy, unavailable, subscribed, not_configured or invalid; or, with no live account session, to /app/sign-in.

post.description: P2-12 B3: the payment provider’s hosted customer portal (payment details, invoices, cancellation) for the signed-in workspace’s own provider customer, resolved server-side (no customer id or email from the browser). Form field: csrf. Same-origin requests with the session’s CSRF token and a sign-in within the last 12 hours only. Cancellation there ends the subscription at the provider; the plan returns to Free only from its verified state.

post.description: Claims a no-signup trial for the signed-in developer account. Form fields: csrf (the page’s token) and management_credential (the trial’s sess_mg_… credential, in the form body only, never in a URL). Same-origin requests with the session’s CSRF token only; the Sess link can never claim. A claim records the account as the trial’s owner, once: nothing moves, the trial keeps its deadlines, limits and deletion time, its receipts stay as issued and its management credential keeps working. The account’s API keys can then read (only read) the trial’s Sessions with the owner read routes, each Session until its result_available_until (as with the management credential). Claiming the same trial again from the same account answers as the first claim.

post.description: The no-signup trial. Without Authorization: creates a trial workspace and its first interactive Session, and returns the management credential once, in the body. With `Authorization: Bearer <management credential>`: creates a further Session in that trial. Interactive Sessions only (mode interactive); no return channel, webhook or outbound endpoint exists for a trial. Trial limits (published, reversible): human link and action window 1 hour; result readable 24 hours after the action window; at most 3 active Sessions and 10 Sessions per trial within its 24-hour creation window; at most 3 new trials per client and 200 overall per rolling 24 hours. Any other credential, or a management credential that is unknown, expired, revoked or bound to one Session → 404 NOT_FOUND. An Idempotency-Key header is refused (400 INVALID_SCHEMA): the credential and the Sess link cannot be replayed.

post.description: Creates a display Session (mode display, source.kind data) or an interactive one (mode interactive, source.kind sess_surface; components: SurfaceComponent). An unrecognized component type → 400 UNKNOWN_COMPONENT; a field-schema keyword outside the supported subset → 400 INVALID_SCHEMA. An Idempotency-Key header is refused (400 INVALID_SCHEMA): the Sess link cannot be replayed (it is stored only as a hash). Retention: the Sess link expires 720 hours after creation with the deployment owner key and 168 hours with a developer API key (free plan). The Session’s content, accepted results and receipts are purged 720 hours (owner key) or 168 hours (developer API key) after the earlier of its completion and its link’s expiry, and outstanding webhook deliveries are cancelled; afterwards every owner route answers 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND. A webhook already delivered is not recalled. Advanced: expires_in (seconds from creation, at least 30, at most the plan’s live-link lifetime) sets a shorter Sess link; the Session’s retention then also ends sooner, because it counts from the earlier of completion and the link’s end. An interactive link of 72000 seconds or less can be extended by the person, at most ten times, up to a fixed horizon (GET /v1/sessions/{id}: action_expires_horizon); its link ends at that horizon, or at the deadline once no extension is left. The response’s action_expires_at is the stored expiry, the same value GET /v1/sessions/{id} returns. Advanced: invocation_id ties the Session to the run of your registered agent that it serves; the archival core of each receipt it issues then binds that agent (target) and its version.

get.description: The Session. Interactive Sessions return status, the current revision, its response_schema and every accepted response bound to its revision; repeated reads of an unchanged Session are byte-identical. Every Session carries action_expires_at, its Sess link’s stored deadline; a read never extends it. It also carries link_state (live, lapsed or expired, at the time of the read), action_expires_horizon and extensions_used: for an interactive link of 20 hours or less, the person may extend the deadline up to ten times, never past the fixed horizon. A lapsed link accepts no answer but can still be extended: the Session is still open, so keep waiting; revoke the link for a hard end at the deadline. extensions lists every accepted extension (old and new deadline, from lapsed, when; no answer value), in order. The ETag is the owner mutations’ concurrency token (the revision and the Event sequence), not a cache validator: it does not change with link timing. A developer API key also reads the Sessions of trials its account claimed (read-only), each until that Session’s result_available_until.

200.description: The current revision of the Session.

Sess-Workspace-Id.description: The authorized Session resource’s actual workspace, including the original trial workspace when read through a claim. It can differ from the API credential’s workspace. Use as trusted receipt audience context, not as a human identity or permission to execute an operation. Absent on errors.

Display Sessions have none. Beside the Events, link_extensions lists every accepted extension of the Sess link (its old and new deadline, whether it was asked for after the deadline, and when; no answer value), in order. post.description: The human form submission (the Sess link is the capability; never log it). Accepted only from the page itself: Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin, or without Fetch Metadata an Origin equal to the public origin. The server resolves action_id from the exact stored revision and validates data against its response_schema. Success is a 303 redirect to the same link; refusals are HTML pages whose stable code is in a data-error-code attribute (422 and 409 re-render the form with the safe draft for explicit resubmit).

303.description: See Other (Post/Redirect/Get): accepted (with a signed decision receipt stored with its Event, returned by the owner GET and the Event log), or a repeated client_event_id with the same request (the original Event and the same receipt, never re-signed). No body. Location is the same Sess link path, relative, with no query: never an Event ID, receipt or submitted data. A GET there renders the Session as it is then: waiting for the agent (responded), the next revision’s form (active) or the completion (completed).

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin submission.

404.description: Unknown, lapsed, expired or revoked link (generic): an answer is accepted only while the link is live.

409.description: SESSION_REVISION_CONFLICT (the current revision, prefilled with the safe draft), RESPONSE_LIMIT_REACHED, SESSION_COMPLETED or IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

422.description: VALIDATION_FAILED: the form with field errors.

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: the receipt keys are not configured; nothing is accepted.

post.description: Asks for more time on a Sess link of 20 hours or less (the Sess link is the capability; never log it). It is the answer form’s second submitter, so the body is the form’s own entries without action_id; same-origin only, as for the answer. While the link is live the deadline (action_expires_at) moves to min(horizon, deadline + step); while it is lapsed (past the deadline, before the horizon, extensions left) to min(horizon, now + step), where step = min(original lifetime, 1 hour). At most ten extensions; never past the fixed horizon. A repeated client_event_id is answered as the original and never counted twice. It never accepts an answer, dispatches, completes the Session or signs a receipt, and never stores or logs a submitted value: the values are only used to re-render the same form.

200.description: Extended (or a repeated request for an extension already made): the current page, its form re-rendered with the submitted values.

400.description: INVALID_SCHEMA: not the form’s exact shape, or values that do not decode.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin request.

404.description: Unknown, expired, revoked or purged link (the one generic page). Nothing changes.

409.description: Nothing changed: SESSION_REVISION_CONFLICT (the current revision, prefilled with the safe draft), SESSION_COMPLETED, or no extension left (none for this link, all ten used, or the deadline already at the horizon; the link stays live until its deadline).

post.description: P2-13 V3 / P2-11, step 1 of "Keep your receipt" (DOCS/spec/keep-v1.md). The human link is the capability; never log it. Sent by the receipt card’s same-origin script after the person taps Keep: Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin (or, without Fetch Metadata, an Origin equal to the page’s origin), application/json, at most 65536 bytes, at most 128 grants. Each round is authorized only by its own receipt-scoped Keep grant: the Session, a receipt list or another round’s grant never authorize it. Reads one Session snapshot (its Event sequence cutoff) and, when some authorized receipt in custody has no holder yet, records one fresh challenge (5 minutes) bound to exactly that batch. Headers as every /s/* response (no-store, no-referrer, noindex, no CORS).

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin request.

404.description: Unknown, expired or revoked link, or a display Session (the generic not-found page, text/html); or NOT_FOUND (JSON, reason no_authorized_rounds) when none of the presented grants authorizes an accepted round of this Session.

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (receipt keys not configured, Keep is off, or the restriction/deletion suppression is not yet re-applied after start)

post.description: P2-13 V3 / P2-11, step 2: the kept-conversation file (DOCS/spec/keep-v1.md), the one bounded, versioned file the person saves — every authorized accepted round of the Session through the snapshot cutoff with its unchanged receipt and bundle (or content unavailable once purged), preservation status (the witness state at snapshot time, with the evidence attached by then), holder status and an inventory. Same request checks as the challenge. With `enrollment`, first enrolls one fresh holder key per receipt of the challenge’s exact batch (or only its final receipt: the disclosed fallback): every proof is checked, then all enrollments and the challenge’s consumption commit atomically; the same request again is an idempotent replay, a different one is refused, a receipt keeps its first holder and a key holds one receipt. Without `enrollment` (key generation or storage failed, or nothing to enrol) the file is exported with every round marked unenrolled: export never depends on enrollment. The file holds no private key, grant secret or Sess link. Content-Disposition: attachment.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin request.

404.description: The generic not-found page for an unknown, expired or revoked link (text/html); or NOT_FOUND (JSON, reason no_authorized_rounds).

409.description: IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT: the challenge was already used by a different request.

422.description: HOLDER_ENROLLMENT_REFUSED with reason challenge_unknown, challenge_expired, batch_mismatch, not_authorized, proof_invalid, key_reused or already_enrolled: nothing was enrolled; the same grants without `enrollment` still export the file.

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (receipt keys not configured, Keep is off, or the restriction/deletion suppression is not yet re-applied after start)

post.description: P2-15 PR-B, Save to Sess from a human page on another origin than /personal (DOCS/spec/personal-copies-v1.md §7). The Sess link is the capability; never log it. Sent by the receipt card’s same-origin script once the Save sheet on the personal origin is signed in and has sent its destination binding: Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin (or an Origin equal to the page’s), application/json, at most 65536 bytes, rate limited per link. Records one pending claim bound to the rounds the presented Keep grants authorize now, exactly as Keep reads them (restricted or deleted rounds never included; no client-chosen IDs), their cutoff, a fresh 256-bit transfer secret (stored as its hash), the purpose, the personal origin, the source verifier’s challenge and the destination binding. The claim expires in 5 minutes. Nothing is saved until the sheet redeems it. Headers as every /s/* response.

201.description: The claim’s transfer secret and expiry.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: not a same-origin request.

404.description: The generic not-found page for an unknown, expired or revoked link (text/html); or NOT_FOUND (JSON, reason no_authorized_rounds).

409.description: IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (reason destination_used): this destination binding already has a claim.

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: the restriction/deletion suppression is not yet re-applied after start.

get.description: The read-only status of a Sess link, for its waiting page (S2): the current revision and the person’s view of the state, nothing else (no owner data, Event IDs, receipts, responses or Surface content). The Sess link is the capability; never log it. Nothing is written or consumed. The waiting page’s same-origin script calls it about every 4 s while the page waits, and navigates to the same link (a GET) once the revision or the state differs. A page with a form also calls it, about every 25 s while visible, only to keep its connection in use: it ignores the answer. Headers as every /s/* response: Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, no CORS.

200.description: waiting: the response to this revision is recorded and the agent has not continued; active: a revision awaits a response; completed: terminal.

404.description: Unknown, expired or revoked link, or a display Session (the generic not-found page).

429.description: RATE_LIMITED: more than 60 status reads of this link in one minute (per runtime process). Retry-After gives the seconds to wait.

get.description: P2-12: the developer workspace’s plan, resolved Sessions used in the current period, the next reset, active Sessions and the 80%/100% allowance warnings. Read only. A resolved Session is one the owner completed after at least one accepted response whose final result was accepted by the webhook endpoint or fetched with an owner credential (a read or completion response sent in full) before its delivery deadline (completion plus the Session’s retention); it counts once, in the period it qualifies. Periods are monthly from the workspace’s billing anchor (its creation on Free). Admission reserves one unit per admitted interactive Session that can still qualify, so admitted work always fits the allowance. Workspaces without a plan (the deployment owner key) → 404 NOT_FOUND.

404.description: NOT_FOUND: this credential’s workspace has no plan

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: billing is not configured

post.description: P2-12: a hosted Checkout for upgrading the developer workspace to a paid plan, at the server’s approved price for that plan (the caller names only the plan). Idempotent: while a Checkout for this plan is open, every request (concurrent or retried) returns the same one; a Checkout for the other plan is ended first, so at most one is payable (it is replaced only after the provider confirms its expiry), and a paid Checkout fences the workspace until its subscription is recorded. A workspace with a subscription gets no new Checkout (409 SUBSCRIPTION_EXISTS: plan changes happen in place). Returning from the Checkout page grants nothing: the plan changes only when the provider’s signed subscription state says it is paid, and the Usage page shows “processing” until then.

200.description: The hosted Checkout page and when it expires.

404.description: NOT_FOUND: this credential’s workspace has no plan

409.description: SUBSCRIPTION_EXISTS (reason: subscribed, checkout_completed): no new Checkout

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (reason: not_configured, checkout_in_progress, checkout_processing, provider_unavailable, provider_rejected). checkout_processing: a paid Checkout’s subscription is still being confirmed; checkout_in_progress: another Checkout is being created or its expiry is not yet confirmed by the provider. No new Checkout is created in either case. Retry after Retry-After seconds when given; a retry returns the same Checkout.

post.description: P2-12: the payment provider’s signed asynchronous events (provider-to-Sess only; DOCS/spec/billing-provider-v1.md). The signature header is verified over the exact raw body (at most 256 KiB, timestamp within 300 s) before the body is parsed. Each event id is processed once (a duplicate is acknowledged without effect); older subscription states never replace newer ones; unknown event types are acknowledged and ignored. Not configured → 404.

400.description: INVALID_SCHEMA: a verified body that is not a provider event

401.description: UNAUTHORIZED: missing, malformed, stale or mismatched signature

404.description: NOT_FOUND: no billing provider is configured

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (reason: provider_unavailable): not processed; redeliver

put.description: Registers the owner workspace’s webhook endpoint (one return channel). It replaces the current endpoint, whose pending deliveries are not redirected (they fail as endpoint_unavailable; redeliver explicitly), and receives nothing until verified. The first registration also creates the signing secret, returned once. 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE while data-encryption keys are not configured.

400.description: WEBHOOK_INVALID_URL (reason: not_https, port, credentials, fragment, non_public_address, malformed, too_long) or INVALID_SCHEMA

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE

get.description: The endpoint, the signing secrets in force (key IDs only) and delivery counts with the age of the oldest pending delivery.

post.description: POSTs a fresh random challenge to the exact registered URL through the delivery egress policy; the endpoint is verified when it echoes it, for 30 days (verification_expires_at). Verifying again renews it; an expired verification reads as pending (no new deliveries; queued ones fail endpoint_unavailable). Every connection resolves the host and refuses non-public addresses.

200.description: Verified; the updated endpoint and its verification expiry.

409.description: WEBHOOK_NOT_CONFIGURED

422.description: WEBHOOK_VERIFICATION_FAILED (reason: egress_refused, redirect, rejected, bad_answer, timeout, connection, dns)

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE

409.description: WEBHOOK_NOT_CONFIGURED

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE

get.description: Every webhook delivery job of the Session’s accepted responses with every attempt (outcome and HTTP status), including permanent failures and exhausted retries.

404.description: SESSION_NOT_FOUND

post.description: Queues the accepted Event for delivery again to the current verified endpoint, with a fresh retry budget. The message is the same bytes (same event_id and receipt). A delivery already pending for the Event to the current endpoint is returned instead; one pending for a replaced endpoint is ended (endpoint_unavailable) and a new one queued.

202.description: Queued, or the existing pending delivery for the same Event/endpoint.

403.description: ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: a Session of a claimed trial (read-only)

404.description: NOT_FOUND (no such accepted Event in this Session)

409.description: WEBHOOK_NOT_CONFIGURED (no verified endpoint)

get.description: The deliberate export of one accepted response as a bundle-v1 disclosure (DOCS/spec/bundle-v1.md): its stored receipt exactly as issued, the complete normalized Surface of the revision it was accepted on, the accepted data, and the current public receipt keys. Never a private key, owner credential or Sess link. Anyone holding the bundle can verify it (POST /v1/receipts/verify, or offline with trusted keys); share it only with whom you mean to show the decision. Read-only. Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform; Referrer-Policy: no-referrer.

400.description: INVALID_SCHEMA (event_id is not an Event ID)

404.description: SESSION_NOT_FOUND, or NOT_FOUND when the Session has no such accepted response with a receipt (or its content was purged)

409.description: EVIDENCE_RESTRICTED: the receipt’s custody record is restricted; nothing is disclosed until it is unrestricted (P2-13 V5)

410.description: EVIDENCE_DELETED: the receipt’s custody record was deleted; only its tombstone remains (P2-13 V5)

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (receipt keys not configured, or restriction/deletion suppression not yet re-applied after start)

post.description: Public, no credential. Verifies a disclosed bundle-v1 against this server's own receipt issuer and published keys (never keys in the bundle) at the current time: the receipt by the receipt-v1 rules, then that the disclosed Surface and input match the receipt hashes. It looks nothing up and stores nothing. The declared signed context is checked only against itself, so context is "unchecked" and application_purpose is "unchecked": check the event, Session and workspace you expect in your own application. A valid result means the issuer accepted this input from someone holding the Sess link; it never names a person or proves that anything was executed. An invalid bundle is a 200 result with valid false and a reason. Body: application/json, at most 2097152 bytes (413 above); 1 MiB canonical bundle bound (reason oversized). Rate limited per client and in total (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After). An absolute 2-second deadline runs from the request's arrival and covers receiving the body as well as verifying it: an unanswered request then gets 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with Connection: close and the connection is closed. Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform; Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; CORS only for the product site origins. Never put a bundle or receipt in a URL.

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (receipt keys not configured, or the 2-second deadline from arrival passed; Connection: close)

post.description: Public, no credential. Verifies an archival envelope (DOCS/spec/archival-core-v1.md §3) with the successor archival verifier against this server's own configuration only: its published receipt keys, its receipt issuer as the expected context issuer, its published witness key set (/.well-known/sess-witness-keys.json) and, when configured, its TUF-verified witness trusted root. Nothing in the request is trusted. It reports the independent dimensions of archival-core-v1 §5 (signature, contents, context, witness, key_trust, live_expiry) with the same statuses and reasons as @sess.si/sdk/archival, and their presentation. The body is the envelope only: contents is therefore unverifiable: content_unavailable (verify a bundle-v1 at /v1/receipts/verify for content), and context is at most incomplete (application_context_unchecked). Without a witness trusted root, attached evidence is indeterminate: witness_trust_unavailable. It looks nothing up and stores nothing. A malformed or oversized envelope is a 200 result. The bundle route is unchanged. Body: application/json, at most 2097152 bytes (413 above); 65,536 bytes envelope bound (reason oversized). The same per-client and total rate limits as /v1/receipts/verify, shared with it (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After), and the same absolute 2-second deadline from the request's arrival (503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with Connection: close). Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform; Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; CORS only for the product site origins. Never put an envelope or receipt in a URL.

200.description: The archival verification result and its presentation.

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (receipt keys not configured, or the 2-second deadline from arrival passed; Connection: close)

post.description: Registers an HTTP Agent Target in the owner workspace (from the credential only). Requires the explicit type http, an https endpoint on port 443 (no user info or fragment; an IP literal must be public), a versioned capability with a bounded input schema, a grant policy (audience origins and lifetime), a budget and an optional enabled switch. Starts are possible only after domain verification. Human, trial and probe credentials cannot register or modify targets. An optional Idempotency-Key makes a retry safe: the same request returns the original target.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Scoped to the owner credential and the operation. The same canonical request body returns the original 201 (status, Location and body: the target as first registered) and registers nothing more, even after the target or the plan changed; a different body with the same key → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; concurrent requests with one key register one target. Only successful registrations are recorded. Without the header every request registers.

Disabling refuses new starts at once and fails admitted runs not yet dispatched (target_disabled); a new version makes older grants stale (409 TARGET_VERSION_CONFLICT on start) and fails admitted runs not yet dispatched (stale_binding). Runs already dispatched are not recalled.

Not part of the versioned binding: the version does not change and admitted runs continue. The card answers 404 unless the target is shared, enabled and verified, lists the site origin among its grant audiences and accepts an empty start input; unsharing or disabling makes it 404 at once, and admission refuses every grant the card issued while the target is not shared. Start and completion counts stay owner-only (TargetResponse.counts).

Never calls the capability endpoint.

post.description: The deliberate start: one transaction checks the grant (live, unrevoked, from its audience Origin) and the target (enabled, verified, same version and capability), validates the input, reserves global, workspace, target, grant and client-bucket limits, records the Invocation with its request identity and an audit event, and enqueues its dispatch. Target, endpoint, capability and policy come only from the grant; any other body field is refused. The same request_id and body returns the same run (200) with the same participant credential; a different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. GET never starts work. Initial limits: 10 active runs globally and per workspace, 1 per grant, 10 starts per client per 24 h, the target’s own budget; a 15-minute run lifetime; input at most 4 KiB. An operator switch refuses every start (503, reason admission_disabled). A target whose workspace is at its plan limit starts nothing new (429, reason workspace_paused); its admitted runs finish.

get.description: P2-13 V6: the custody records of the owner workspace (from the credential only), newest first: archival custody by workspace sequence, or (custody=exception) the receipts held unverified, by acceptance time. Minimal metadata only; a list never carries a receipt, a Surface or an answer. Filters: target_id (records whose archival core binds that target; records with no target binding never match) and accepted_from/accepted_to. Every answer is labelled "issued records in this defined scope/range" with complete_history false: it is never a complete history. Cursor-paginated (next_cursor). Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform.

parameters.description: UTC instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fff]Z, at most millisecond precision; finer is refused), inclusive.

parameters.name: accepted_to

post.description: P2-13 V6: a deliberate, bounded export of one explicit range of the owner workspace’s custody records: both from_sequence and to_sequence (archival), or both accepted_from and accepted_to. At most limit (≤ 100) records and 8 MiB; a range beyond either is truncated and range.next_cursor continues it. Each record carries its exact receipt, its archival envelope (signed core and preservation evidence) and preservation status; the original Surface and input only while still retained, otherwise content {status: unavailable, reason: purged} (never reconstructed). Exception-custody records are labelled unverified. The document carries a disclosure warning and the scope label "issued records in this defined scope/range" (never a complete history). Content-Disposition: attachment; the filename is built from the workspace, custody and range only. At most 6 exports per workspace per 10 minutes. The export’s content is never logged.

get.description: P2-13 V5: the status of one custody record of the owner workspace (from the credential only), never its content: available, restricted (with its reason code and since when) or deleted (with its reason code and deletion time). A restricted or deleted record is excluded from the list, the export, its bundle and every other receipt-scoped fetch; a restricted one stays verifiable for preservation integrity. Restriction, holds and deletion are decided by the operator through the recorded procedure (DOCS/spec/custody-restriction-deletion-v1.md); holds are not shown here. A deletion does not recall exported copies or files people already kept, and the public witness commitment (an aggregate batch root) remains. Another workspace’s record, or an unknown event ID, is 404. Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform.

Verify a receipt (compact JWS, typ sess-receipt+jwt) with the key its protected header kid names. Expected issuer: configured SESS_RECEIPT_ISSUER, otherwise the origin of SESS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Expected audience: the Session’s actual workspace, from independently trusted configuration or Sess-Workspace-Id on authenticated owner create/retrieve. Claimed trials retain their original workspace. No credential. 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE while the receipt keys are not configured. Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform.

The current key has valid_to null; a rotated-out key is kept with its closed window, so evidence it signed stays verifiable. Read with parseWitnessKeySet and pass as the witnessKeys anchor of verifyWitnessEvidence, beside an independently distributed trusted root. Public keys only. No credential. Empty keys when no witness key is configured; 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE when a configured key set is unusable (it is never trimmed or served empty). Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform.

get.description: This document: the generated, CI-drift-checked contract of the artifact.
Process liveness only: no dependency is called. Cache-Control: no-store.

Concurrent requests share the check in progress; the next request after it settles runs a new one. Never migrates and never calls a telemetry backend. Query parameters are ignored. Cache-Control: no-store.

Answers 200 even when readiness does not. git_sha, build_id and build_time are each null when not supplied or invalid (git_sha: SESS_GIT_SHA missing, empty or malformed; build_time also while it is more than 5 s in the future, checked per request); any null fails readiness (503).
